title: How Many Martian Meteorites Are Really on Earth?
description: Earlier surveys recorded only 277 rocks from Mars, a figure that continues to populate outdated articles. Thanks to recent recoveries in deserts across the globe, researchers have cataloged approximately 435 confirmed specimens. The true collection of Martian material on Earth is substantially larger than most people realize.
narration: MARTIAN METEORITE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK Most reference books still cite an old count of 277 rocks knocked loose from Mars. You picture a frozen scientific archive, but that widely circulated tally is completely out of date. That 277 figure reflects a September 2020 census of classified specimens. Since then, fresh finds across desert sands—including an ancient four-billion-year-old rock from Mali named Teghaza 001—have driven the verified global tally to roughly 435 Martian stones. Earth holds far more pieces of Mars than older records report.
